candidates.behaviour: The sink accepts a pending word 8'h3C (m_axis_tvalid and m_axis_tready both high) on the same clock that a second good frame completes. On the next clock m_axis_tvalid is high with m_axis_tdata 8'hA5, so both words are delivered and the second is not lost. The RTL also pulses overrun_error on that clock, because overrun_error_reg samples the old m_axis_tvalid_reg, even though the old word was read; the README says overrun should pulse only when a word was not read. The gold should report this.
candidates.title: rx_accept_old_word_same_cycle_new_word_lands
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline sink is always ready, so a pending word is never still unread at the exact clock the next frame completes.

candidates.behaviour: A frame ends with a low stop bit, so frame_error pulses. rxd stays low from that pulse until busy rises again, so the receiver treats the low level as the next start bit. That frame completes and m_axis_tvalid rises with m_axis_tdata 8'hA5.
candidates.title: rx_resync_after_frame_error
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never sends a frame with a low stop bit, so the receiver never has to resynchronise after a framing error.

candidates.behaviour: After the receiver delivers a word (m_axis_tvalid rises), the next start bit is picked up within two clocks. That is, busy goes high again no more than two clocks after the stop-bit sample. The second frame then completes with m_axis_tvalid high and m_axis_tdata 8'h5A, and frame_error stays low. A twin cover checks the three-clock case.
candidates.title: rx_short_stop_bit_back_to_back
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline always drives a full-length stop bit, so the next start edge comes about half a bit after the stop sample, never immediately.

candidates.behaviour: During a data bit (bit_cnt between 2 and 9), the synchronised input rxd_reg changes level and changes back while prescale_reg is non-zero, so the glitch lies away from the mid-bit sample point. The frame still completes with m_axis_tvalid rising, m_axis_tdata 8'hA5 and no frame_error.
candidates.title: rx_glitch_off_sample_point_ignored
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline drives clean bits with no mid-bit transitions on rxd.

candidates.behaviour: The receiver delivers m_axis_tdata 8'hA5 from a frame received with prescale 1. prescale is then changed to 3 while busy is low. The next frame is delivered with m_axis_tdata 8'h5A and frame_error stays low.
candidates.title: rx_prescale_change_between_frames
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline uses a fixed prescale of 5, so the run-time prescale input never changes and prescale[1] never toggles.

candidates.behaviour: The transmitter sends one byte with prescale 1, and prescale is then changed to 3 while busy is low. The next byte, 8'h5A, is shifted out on txd with every data bit lasting 24 clocks: at each data-bit boundary, prescale_reg reaches 0 with txd holding the matching bit of 8'h5A.
candidates.title: tx_prescale_change_between_frames
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline transmits only at a fixed prescale of 5, so prescale[1] never toggles and no frame follows a rate change.

candidates.behaviour: With m_axis_tready low throughout and no handshake, three good frames complete in a row. overrun_error pulses when the second frame completes and pulses again when the third completes. At that second overrun_error pulse, m_axis_tvalid is high and m_axis_tdata is 8'h5A.
candidates.title: rx_double_overrun_third_word
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline sink is always ready, so overrun_error never toggles.

candidates.behaviour: overrun_error pulses while m_axis_tready is low. The next handshake after it, with m_axis_tvalid and m_axis_tready both high, transfers m_axis_tdata 8'hC3, the word whose frame caused the overrun. No further overrun_error occurs in between.
candidates.title: rx_overrun_then_accept_newest
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never stalls the sink, so it has no overrun and no accept after one.

candidates.behaviour: m_axis_tvalid is high holding 8'h3C and m_axis_tready is low when a frame ends with a low stop bit. frame_error pulses while m_axis_tvalid stays high, m_axis_tdata is still 8'h3C and overrun_error is low.
candidates.title: rx_frame_error_with_pending_word
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never sends a bad stop bit and never stalls the sink.

candidates.behaviour: m_axis_tvalid rises while m_axis_tready is low. On the very next clock m_axis_tready is high, so the word 8'hA5 is accepted after exactly one stall cycle. A twin cover checks the two-stall-cycle case.
candidates.title: rx_single_cycle_stall_accept
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline holds m_axis_tready high permanently.

candidates.behaviour: With prescale held at 16'd1 from the start bit onward (8-clock bits, start reload of 2), m_axis_tvalid rises with m_axis_tdata 8'h96 and frame_error stays low throughout the frame.
candidates.title: rx_min_prescale_word
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline only uses prescale 5.

candidates.behaviour: With prescale held at 16'd2, two consecutive words are delivered: m_axis_tdata 8'h12, then 8'h34. frame_error stays low in between.
candidates.title: rx_prescale2_two_words
candidates.why_baseline_misses: prescale[1] never toggles in the baseline (prescale 5).

candidates.behaviour: After a frame_error pulse, the receiver goes idle: busy is low and rxd is high for at least 16 consecutive clocks. The next frame then delivers m_axis_tdata 8'hA5 with m_axis_tvalid rising, and frame_error stays low.
candidates.title: rx_recover_after_frame_error_idle
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never produces a frame error, so it never recovers from one.

candidates.behaviour: A word 8'hA5 has already been accepted, so m_axis_tvalid is low and m_axis_tdata is 8'hA5. A frame with data_reg 8'h5A then ends with a low stop bit. frame_error pulses, m_axis_tvalid stays low and m_axis_tdata remains 8'hA5, so the bad word is discarded.
candidates.title: rx_frame_error_keeps_old_tdata
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never sends a low stop bit.

candidates.behaviour: m_axis_tvalid holds 8'h3C, stalled by m_axis_tready low. The sink accepts it while busy is high and bit_cnt is between 2 and 9 of the next frame. That frame later completes with m_axis_tvalid rising, m_axis_tdata 8'hA5 and overrun_error low.
candidates.title: rx_accept_during_next_frame
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline sink never stalls, so it never accepts a stalled word in the middle of a frame.

candidates.behaviour: m_axis_tvalid is high holding 8'h3C with m_axis_tready low and no handshake. First, a bad frame makes frame_error pulse. Then a good frame completes, overrun_error pulses and m_axis_tdata becomes 8'hA5.
candidates.title: rx_frame_error_then_overrun
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never produces either error strobe.

candidates.behaviour: rst is sampled high on exactly the clock where a good frame's stop bit is sampled (prescale_reg 0, bit_cnt 1, rxd_reg high) while m_axis_tvalid is low. m_axis_tvalid stays low for that frame. After rst is released, a new frame delivers m_axis_tdata 8'h5A.
candidates.title: rx_rst_at_stop_sample
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline only resets while the receiver is idle.

candidates.behaviour: m_axis_tvalid is high holding 8'h3C with m_axis_tready low when a start bit is rejected (prescale_reg 0, bit_cnt 10, rxd_reg high). m_axis_tvalid stays high and overrun_error stays low. The next handshake then transfers m_axis_tdata 8'h3C.
candidates.title: rx_pending_word_survives_false_start
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never sends a false start and never stalls the sink.

candidates.behaviour: A pending word 8'h3C is accepted, with m_axis_tvalid and m_axis_tready both high, on the same clock that frame_error is high. On the next clock m_axis_tvalid is low and m_axis_tdata is still 8'h3C.
candidates.title: rx_accept_coincides_with_frame_error
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline has no frame errors and no stalled words.

candidates.behaviour: s_axis_tvalid rises on exactly the clock where the transmitter ends its stop period (prescale_reg 0, bit_cnt 0) while s_axis_tready is low. txd is low on the next clock and s_axis_tready is high, and the byte shifted out is 8'hC3. A twin cover checks tvalid rising one clock later.
candidates.title: tx_tvalid_rises_on_frame_end_cycle
candidates.why_baseline_misses: In the baseline, s_axis_tvalid either stays high back-to-back or rises long after the frame ends; it never rises on that exact clock.

candidates.behaviour: s_axis_tvalid is high on the first clock after rst falls, while s_axis_tready is still low. The byte is loaded on that clock, so txd goes low on the next clock and s_axis_tready is high. The byte is then shifted out as 8'hA5.
candidates.title: tx_tvalid_first_clock_after_reset
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline waits two clocks after reset release before asserting s_axis_tvalid.

candidates.behaviour: With prescale held at 16'd1, uart_tx shifts a byte out with every data bit lasting 8 clocks. Sampled at the eight data-bit boundaries, txd forms 8'h96.
candidates.title: tx_min_prescale_word
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline only uses prescale 5.

candidates.behaviour: With prescale held at 16'd2 and s_axis_tvalid kept high, bytes 8'h12 and then 8'h34 are shifted out on txd in consecutive frames, with busy high continuously between them.
candidates.title: tx_prescale2_two_bytes
candidates.why_baseline_misses: prescale[1] never toggles in the baseline.

candidates.behaviour: With prescale 16'd1 and back-to-back frames, the last data bit is 0. txd is then high for exactly 9 clocks (8*prescale+1) between the start of the stop bit and the next start bit. Twin covers check 8 and 10 clocks.
candidates.title: tx_back_to_back_stop_length_prescale1
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline back-to-back traffic is only at prescale 5.

candidates.behaviour: While busy is high and bit_cnt is between 1 and 8, s_axis_tvalid rises after having been low since the last handshake. It holds s_axis_tdata 8'h3C stable until the byte is loaded, and the next frame shifts out 8'h3C.
candidates.title: tx_tvalid_rises_mid_frame
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never raises s_axis_tvalid while a frame is in progress after a gap.

candidates.behaviour: With prescale 16'd3 and s_axis_tvalid low, busy falls and s_axis_tready rises on the same clock. That clock comes exactly 25 clocks after bit_cnt went from 1 to 0 (start of the stop bit). Twin covers check 24 and 26 clocks.
candidates.title: tx_busy_fall_and_ready_after_stop_prescale3
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline only runs at prescale 5.

candidates.behaviour: Toggle holes prescale[3], prescale[4] and prescale[5] on uart_rx and uart_tx. Like W3, they are closed trivially by any prescale of 8 or more. That is outside the formal bound (prescale 1..4), and they carry no behaviour beyond the large-prescale items R7 and T2.
candidates.title: prescale_bits_3_to_5_toggle
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline uses prescale 5 only.
